svg.title: mdv readme.md
svg.text: A minimal markdown viewer for the terminal.
standard output and exits: no full-screen interface, no keys to learn. At a
terminal, a long document opens in your pager (
, and a short one is simply
printed. Piped output stays plain text, so
[image: This readme as mdv prints it at 80 columns]
Colors come from your terminal's own theme. mdv sends only text attributes
(bold, italic, dim, underline, strikethrough) and, at most, one of the sixteen
palette colors, never a color of its own. Links with a web address are real
in terminals that support them; a relative one shows its path after
bold, lists and quotes are indented under their markers,
and code blocks sit behind a thin gutter without being reflowed. Text wraps by
display width, so wide characters such as 日本語 and emoji such as 🌿 take the
room they really take. From GitHub's dialect it adds
tildes, task lists with a box in place of each bullet, and tables drawn in light
box lines. A table too wide for the terminal wraps its longest cells, and when
even that would break words, each row is listed as one line per column.
mdv has only been tried on macOS so far. If something looks wrong in your
terminal on Linux or elsewhere, a report is welcome.
renders both, each headed by its name.
wraps at N columns, past 80 if you like
keeps the styles in a pipe, or drops them
prints each link's address after its text, as
draws bullets, gutters, rules, boxes and table
describes every option, how each element looks, and what
mdv does with paging, colors and width.
• CommonMark 0.31.2, passing all 652 examples of its spec
mdv builds with Zig 0.17.0 through 0.18.0-dev.954+60635c2bd, a development
build, and other versions may not compile.
zig build # a debug binary in zig-out/bin/mdv
zig build test spec # the unit tests and the spec examples
zig build run -- FILE # runs it without installing
zig build golden -- --update # redraws the picture above, among others
